title: DimCL: Dimension-Aware Augmentation in Contrastive Learning for Recommendation

problem.claim: Contrastive learning for recommendation generates augmented views from user-item interaction graphs, but uncontrolled augmentation can introduce hidden dimensions that are noisy or irrelevant to recommendation.

gap.claim: Prior augmentation methods mainly use stochastic functions that perturb hidden dimensions uniformly and lack fine-grained control over dimension-specific noise.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contrastive learning has been successful in addressing data sparsity in collaborative-filtering recommender systems.
Contrastive learning generates different augmented views from a user-item interaction graph.
Existing approaches mainly apply stochastic, uniform perturbations across hidden dimensions, which can introduce harmful and irrelevant dimensions.

Dimension-specific noise is difficult to remove because dimension efficacy for contrastive learning is hard to distinguish and the semantic gap between contrastive learning and recommendation is difficult to bridge.
Ignoring these limitations may produce redundant, false-positive, and irrelevant noise in augmented-view representations.

source_observation.claim: Uniform perturbation across hidden dimensions may introduce noise that is harmful or irrelevant to the downstream recommendation task.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation quality may depend on whether perturbations preserve task-relevant dimension semantics rather than only increasing view diversity.

application.claim: When designing contrastive augmentations for recommendation, evaluate and control perturbations at the representation-dimension level.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether dimension-aware control improves recommendation performance or generalizes beyond this setting.

unknowns: The proposed method and its implementation details are not described.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, experimental results, or quantitative comparisons are supplied.
No theoretical analysis or independent verification is supplied.
